text:
Alex: Heads-up — opened a small Terraform PR to fix NAT/EIP association for the GPU subnets. Needs 1 infra approval before I merge. https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 :eyes:

terraform-bot: PR #482 opened by Alex — terraform plan queued. Checks: fmt, validate, plan.

Maya: taking a look now. quick q — are we intentionally recreating the eip associations vs doing an update?

Alex: good call — it's due to how we moved from inline attachment to aws_eip_association resource. I added a count+depends_on to avoid racy deletes, but plan still shows replacements for two associations.

Samir: FYI CI failed on fmt for one file. run `terraform fmt -diff -check` locally and push. Also plan snippet looks like it will replace the association, paste from my local plan:

```
# aws_eip_association.this[0] will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_eip_association" "this" {
    ~ id        = "eipassoc-0a1b2c3d" -> (known after apply)
      allocation_id = "eipalloc-12345678"
      instance_id   = "i-0abcd1234"
  }
\nPlan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 1 to destroy.
```

Jen: @Samir can you confirm the destroy won't detach EIPs from anything critical? I thought these GPUs are on ephemeral nodes but want to be safe.

Samir: Confirmed — these associations are with the GPU pool NAT gateway for batch workloads. Destroy+create will move associations but public connectivity will be briefly interrupted for instances using the old association. Low risk during maintenance window.

Kevin: SG change in the same PR looks fine to me (just narrow a port on the mgmt sg). Once fmt is fixed I'm happy to approve.

Alex: pushed a fix for fmt and reworked the depends_on to preserve order. Also added a short note in the PR description about expected brief connectivity blip and rollback steps.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #482 — fmt ✅ validate ✅ plan ✅.

Maya: left a small review comment about tags (we should copy the standard infra tags). Alex, can you apply or I can patch?

Alex: patched tags and pushed.

Kevin: Approved.

Samir: Approved — left one nit but not blocking.

Jen: Approved from my side after Samir's confirmation.

Alex: Thanks all. Planning to merge after the 16:00 UTC maintenance window. Will monitor NAT metrics and roll back if errors spike. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: noted — I'll watch for NAT gateway error_rate and route flaps during/after apply and ping here if anything unusual shows up.

Alex: Merge done at 16:12 UTC. Post-apply plan: associations updated, no new allocations.

ops-oncall: initial metrics look clean — small blip during apply, recovered within 30s. Closing the loop.

Alex: great, thanks everyone!
